item.title: Just for the record
item.content:encoded:
I feel it's important to note that I thought of this story in response to the diary-of-an-SCP contest.

I went for a walk in the park by the river, across from my old apartment. I pondered what I could write about. I sat down under a tree, by the circus school, and I thought. And it came to me.

And I thought, and I thought.

And then I walked back to my apartment and wrote the whole thing in 15 minutes.

The "sitting under a tree in the park, out by the circus school" image is very strong to me when I think about how I came to write this story.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
She writes down the answers on the IQ test because those are the answers she sees on the future version of the page. Even if she doesn't know what the answers to the questions are, she writes them down because they're on the page in the future and that's where she sees them. It's an ontological paradox. She knows that it's not spelled "anti-logical paradock". She doesn't have a choice. She's just tracing.

She writes down "comma" because that's the way it's spelled on the future version of the page. She knows it's not spelled right. She doesn't have a choice. She's just tracing.

She can't even write out her own anger without having it appear on the page beforehand. The "FUCK YOU" part at the end? She has to write it because she saw it in the page's future.

She doesn't have a choice.

She's just tracing.

Understand now?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
She sees what will happen to the paper. She sees exactly what will be on the paper once she is done writing. If she's going to draw a square, she will see a square on the paper, exactly where she was going to draw. She can't not do it. It's what she would have done anyway.

If she looks at the paper and it has scribbles on it, and then she closes her eyes and scribbles on the page at random, her scribbles will exactly match what she saw.

When she puts her pen to the paper, she can already see exactly what marks it will make.

She can't write anything on her own. It's just tracing what she already sees. Even if she wants to, it's just tracing.

She's not compelled to do it, but she knows that she will, because if she didn't do it then she wouldn't see it. It's an ontological paradox, and she fucking hates it.

Am I right in thinking that the thing with this SCP (I have read it but I forget the number) is that she sees what will happen to something/someone? An example from the test log was that she saw a guy not wearing his wedding ring, but he was and his marriage ended soon after…

So she's not compelled to act to make stuff happen, just sees what will be…

Could she not, in that case, just scribble all over the page or write something different?

I may be over annalyzing this as it's a tale… and am more than ready to be riddiculed for this comment.

All that said, it's very well written and I have up voted as I do like the piece. Just adding my 2 pennies.
